questions.question: Which two characteristics make up competent communication?
Appropriateness in communication means achieving your communication goal.
What does it mean to say communication is transactional?

choices.a: People take turns sending and receiving messages
choices.b: Messages only flow from sender to receiver
choices.c: People send and receive messages simultaneously and influence each other
choices.d: Communication only happens through written messages

questions.question: In the communication model, what is encoding?

choices.b: Turning your thoughts into a message
choices.c: The receiver's response to a message
choices.d: Anything that interferes with a message

questions.question: In the communication model, what is feedback?

choices.a: The situation or environment in which communication occurs
choices.b: The way a message is delivered
choices.c: The receiver's response to the message

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four needs that effective communication can satisfy?
Which need does communication satisfy when it helps us develop our sense of self?
Communication satisfies practical needs by helping us accomplish tasks and achieve goals.
Which statement best defines gender?

choices.a: Biological characteristics such as hormones and chromosomes
choices.d: Socially and culturally shaped roles, behaviours, identities, and expressions

questions.question: Sex refers to biological characteristics such as reproductive organs, hormones, and chromosomes.
Which best describes culture?

choices.a: The shared beliefs, values, customs, traditions, and behaviours of a group
choices.c: The language a person speaks at home

questions.question: In cultural safety, who determines whether care is culturally safe?
Which best describes cultural humility?

choices.b: Continuously reflecting on your own biases, recognizing power differences, and learning from others
choices.c: Treating all clients exactly the same

questions.question: Cultural humility is a one-time training that is completed once you understand a culture.
Which describes low-context communication?

choices.a: Messages rely heavily on body language and shared understanding
choices.b: Messages are direct, explicit, and rely mainly on words
choices.c: Messages are communicated mostly through silence
choices.d: Messages depend mainly on the relationship between speakers

questions.question: Which describes high-context communication?

choices.a: Messages rely more on relationships, shared understanding, body language, and context
choices.b: Messages are direct and rely mainly on words

questions.question: High-context communication relies mainly on explicit, spoken words.
What is cultural competence?

choices.d: The ability to understand and work respectfully and effectively with people from different cultural backgrounds

questions.question: Which is a good way to increase your intercultural competence?

choices.a: Assume you already know how people from a culture behave
choices.b: Reflect on your own biases and assumptions
choices.c: Avoid asking questions so you don't offend anyone
choices.d: Only build relationships with people similar to you

questions.question: Stereotyping is an effective way to learn about other cultures.
Which behaviour shows a client that you are actively listening?

choices.a: Checking your phone while they talk
choices.d: Facing them, using open body language, and paraphrasing what they say

questions.question: Which of the following is an open-ended question?
Closed-ended questions are best for encouraging clients to give detailed answers.
Which best defines caring?

choices.a: Completing tasks as quickly as possible
choices.b: Making decisions for clients to protect them
choices.c: Showing concern for another person's well-being

questions.question: A client says, "I am so sick and tired of my body not working the way it used to. I hate having to ask for help all the time." Which is the best paraphrasing response?

choices.a: "You should be grateful that help is available."
choices.b: "It sounds like you're frustrated by the changes in your body and having to depend on others for help."
choices.c: "Everyone gets old, so try not to worry."
choices.d: "Would you like to take a nap?"

questions.question: Which best defines self-concept?

choices.a: How much a person likes themselves
choices.c: How a person sees and understands themselves

questions.question: Self-concept is described as "dynamic." What does this mean?

choices.a: It can change over time as we gain new experiences
choices.c: It is the same in every situation
choices.d: It is based only on what others say

questions.question: Self-concept is organized, meaning different beliefs about ourselves form an overall picture of who we are.
Which is a characteristic of someone with positive self-esteem?

choices.c: They depend on constant praise from others
choices.d: They accept their strengths and weaknesses

questions.question: Which theory suggests we develop our self-image partly by imagining how others see and judge us?
Which theory, associated with Leon Festinger, says we evaluate ourselves by comparing our abilities and traits with others?
Which is an example of showing warmth as an HCA?

choices.a: Greeting clients with a smile and a gentle, respectful tone
choices.c: Avoiding eye contact to give clients privacy

questions.question: It is acceptable to joke about a client's condition if the client seems to be in a good mood.
Which is a guideline for using humour at work?

choices.a: Use humour to avoid serious concerns
choices.b: Continue joking even if the client seems uncomfortable
choices.c: Consider the client's culture, feelings, and sense of humour
choices.d: Use the same jokes with every client

questions.question: A loud television in a client's room interferes with a conversation. What type of noise is this?
A client has hearing loss that makes it hard to understand you. What type of noise is this?
A client is so anxious about a test result that they cannot focus on what you are saying. What type of noise is this?
You use medical jargon that a client does not understand. What type of noise is this?
Which best describes active listening?

choices.a: Hearing the words a speaker says
choices.b: Fully concentrating on, understanding, and responding to a speaker
choices.c: Waiting for your turn to speak
choices.d: Giving advice as soon as a problem is mentioned

questions.question: Asking clarifying questions and noticing non-verbal cues are part of active listening.
Why can the same message be received differently by different people?

choices.a: People have different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives
choices.b: Messages change as they travel through the air
choices.c: Only the sender controls the meaning of a message
choices.d: Most people do not pay attention to messages

questions.question: Which of the following can affect how someone receives a message?

choices.a: Only the words that were used
choices.b: Only the sender's tone of voice
choices.d: Culture, past experiences, emotions, and expectations

questions.question: Non-verbal communication is described as "continuous." What does this mean?

choices.a: It only occurs when we are speaking
choices.b: Body language and facial expressions communicate even when we are not speaking
choices.c: It always has the same meaning
choices.d: It never changes during a conversation

questions.question: Non-verbal communication is described as "ambiguous." What does this mean?

choices.b: It is easy to interpret accurately
choices.c: The same gesture or expression can have different meanings depending on the person and context
choices.d: It is less important than verbal communication

questions.question: To communicate trust and care, your non-verbal cues should match your words.
What is the empathy formula?

choices.b: Share a similar experience + offer support
choices.c: Ask a question + wait for an answer
choices.d: Acknowledge the person's feelings + identify the reason for those feelings

questions.question: Which statement best follows the empathy formula?

choices.a: "You sound frustrated because you need more help than before."
choices.b: "Don't be upset, it will get better."

questions.question: Which type of empathy involves understanding another person's perspective and feelings?
Which type of empathy involves understanding and relating to someone's feelings while being motivated to help?
Emotional empathy involves emotionally relating to or sharing another person's feelings.
"Honesty matters to me" is an example of which of the following?
"I believe I can learn new skills" is an example of which of the following?
Which best describes an attitude?

choices.b: A positive or negative feeling or opinion about something

questions.question: Which is something an HCA should consider before using self-disclosure with a client?

choices.a: Whether it will make the HCA feel better
choices.b: Whether the HCA's story is more interesting than the client's
choices.c: Whether it will fill a silence
choices.d: Whether it will benefit the client and is relevant to their situation

questions.question: Self-disclosure is appropriate when it shifts the focus of the conversation to the HCA's own experiences.
